transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep having these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. Like, I’ll worry I left my aunt’s medicine out the wrong way, or that I didn’t set up my classroom materials safely. Even when I know I probably did it right, the doubt keeps coming back into my head.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or trying to neutralize the thought in some way?

Yes. Before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back and check the same things a few times. Like the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans… and sometimes I’ll just replay in my head what I did, to make sure I didn’t miss anything. I usually stop once I feel calm enough to leave, but it can make me run late sometimes.
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah, it does, but I’m still managing. I get to work and take care of family things, but my mornings take longer than they should. Sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or like I’m behind before the day has even started.

And things like lesson prep or even journaling at night don’t feel as smooth or relaxing as they used to. It’s not completely stopping me, but it definitely adds stress.
Do you spend more than an hour each day dealing with these thoughts and checking behaviors?
I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really timed it. It feels like it adds up, especially in the mornings, but I don’t know if it’s more than an hour every day.
